jobs.title: Business Operations
jobs.description:
Who We Are

Physical Intelligence is bringing general-purpose AI into the physical world. We are a group of engineers, scientists, roboticists, and company builders developing foundation models and learning algorithms to power the robots of today and the physically-actuated devices of the future.

As the company scales, success increasingly depends not just on research excellence, but on strong business execution - across partnerships, operations, infrastructure, and deployment.

Success in this role looks like independently identifying the highest-leverage problems, structuring them into executable plans, and driving them to measurable outcomes with minimal founder involvement.

The Team

This role sits close to the founders and works cross-functionally with research, engineering, operations, finance, legal, and external partners. There is no single “lane”, the mandate is to add leverage wherever the company most needs it.

In This Role You Will

- Own and execute cross-functional projects with high ambiguity and real business impact.

- Drive data, compute, and infrastructure partnerships, from sourcing through negotiation and management.

- Plug into deployment efforts: sourcing opportunities, structuring contracts, pricing, and operational setup.

- Assist with and drive internal scaling initiatives such as office expansion, international operations, and company planning.

- Support investor, board, and external communications including decks, analyses, and prep.

- Act as an execution arm for founders and leaders, translating priorities into outcomes.

What We Hope You’ll Bring

- Strong analytical and strategic instincts with a bias toward action.

- Comfort operating independently in ambiguous environments.

- Commercial mindset and basic financial fluency (contracts, pricing, tradeoffs).

- Exceptional written and verbal communication.

- Willingness to do anything, paired with strong prioritization instincts and comfort pushing back when work is low-leverage.

- Strong π-fit: respect for research and engineering culture, curiosity, and intellectual humility.

Bonus Points If You Have

- Background in consulting, venture capital, private equity, or finance.

- Experience negotiating vendor, data, or infrastructure agreements.

- Exposure to startups that have scaled quickly or inflected suddenly.

- International operations or cross-border project experience.



Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

jobs.title: Supply Chain Lead
jobs.description:
Physical Intelligence is bringing general-purpose AI into the physical world. We are a team of engineers, scientists, roboticists, and company builders developing foundation models and learning algorithms to power the robots of today and the physically-actuated devices of the future.

In this role you will own the supply chain and procurement strategy for PI's robot platforms as we scale from prototype to production. You'll build and expand a resilient global supply chain across electromechanical systems including actuators, motors, gearboxes, sensors, compute modules, PCBAs, harnessing, and structural/mechanical assemblies while partnering closely with engineering and manufacturing.

Sitting at the interface between our engineering teams and the industries that supply core technologies, you'll own sourcing strategy and supplier execution across the full robot BOM, lead the transition from in-house builds toward contract manufacturing, negotiate commercial agreements against aggressive cost and quality targets, and establish the sourcing processes, metrics, and supplier performance frameworks for a rapidly scaling robotics organization’s needs.

In this role you will

 - Own sourcing strategy and supplier execution across the full robot BOM: actuators, motors, gearboxes, sensors, compute modules, PCBAs, harnessing, and mechanical / structural assemblies.

 - Establish sourcing processes, supplier selection, capacity planning, dual-sourcing, and risk mitigation. Metrics, and supplier performance management frameworks appropriate for a rapidly scaling robotics organization.

 - Partner closely with mechanical, electrical, firmware, and compute engineering teams to drive design for manufacturability, supply chain resilience, and cost optimization.

 - Ensure material continuity across in-house and outsourced manufacturing. This includes determining order quantities and driving inventory accuracy with manufacturing and production teams.

 - Develop multi-source strategies for critical and allocation-sensitive components (including high-performance compute) and proactively mitigate geopolitical and single-source risks.

 - Negotiate pricing, lead times, allocation, and commercial agreements to meet aggressive cost, quality, and production targets.

 - Lead the transition from prototype and in-house manufacturing toward contract manufacturing, including CM selection, qualification, onboarding, and operational scaling.

 - Support NPI and production ramp activities with suppliers and manufacturing partners across Asia Pacific and other global regions.

What we hope you'll bring

 - Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Supply Chain, Business, Operations, or a related field (it is okay if you have an MBA)

 - 5+ years of experience in strategic sourcing, procurement, or supply chain management for hardware products.

 - Proven track record taking hardware products from prototype through production ramp at scale and either developing a new supply chain or moving it to a new geography.

 - Direct experience sourcing electromechanical components, PCBAs, and high-performance compute systems, as well as motors, actuators, gearboxes, sensors, and mechanical assemblies.

 - Demonstrated success negotiating pricing, lead times, allocation, and commercial agreements to meet aggressive cost, quality, and production targets.

 - Strong quantitative and analytical skills: should-cost and BOM cost modeling, spend analysis, supplier financial research, and cost / capacity scenario analysis and benchmarking.

 - Strong understanding of MRP/ERP systems, inventory planning, and material continuity across in-house and outsourced manufacturing. Familiarity with NPI, DFM/DFA, and manufacturing scale-up workflows.

 - Experience sourcing constrained or allocation-sensitive components (compute, motors, etc)

 - Superb communication and cross-functional relationship-building; ability to influence and drive projects without direct authority.

 - Comfortable operating in a fast-moving, high-ownership environment, with willingness to travel internationally (primarily Asia Pacific).

jobs.title: General Manager, Research Operations
jobs.description:
General Manager, Research Operations

Who We Are

Physical Intelligence is bringing general-purpose AI into the physical world. We are a group of engineers, scientists, roboticists, and company builders developing foundation models and learning algorithms to power the robots of today and the physically-actuated devices of the future.

 

High-quality data is the fuel for that mission. Our operations teams bring together people, robots, environments, and processes to produce the data our models need.

 

The Team

Research Operations supports the hands-on work behind our research, from collecting and evaluating data to testing and deploying our own tools and systems. The work changes quickly as our research evolves, so the team needs to be both highly organized and adaptable. The Research Operations GM leads the people and managers doing this work. They ensure teams are staffed effectively, build strong managers, and create an organization where people can perform at a high level and grow.

 

In this role you will

 - Lead and develop a large operations team and its managers.

 - Own staffing, performance, retention, and day-to-day operations.

 - Make sure people and resources are focused on the highest-priority work.

 - Build training and development programs that improve performance and prepare people for more complex research and deployment work.

 - Use data to identify problems and improve quality, productivity, and how the team operates.

 - Work closely with researchers and engineers to adapt the operation as their needs change.

 

What We Hope You'll Bring

 - 7+ years leading large, high-output operations teams, ideally involving physical or hands-on work.

 - Experience managing and developing managers and team leads.

 - A track record of improving quality, productivity, and retention at scale.

 - Strong judgment around staffing, prioritization, and performance.

 - Experience building teams where strong people stay and grow.

 - Comfort working in a fast-changing, technical environment.

 

Bonus Points

 - Experience in robotics, hardware, manufacturing, logistics, or other complex physical operations.

 - Experience supporting research or engineering teams.

 - Experience building training and career development programs.

 - Experience with data collection, eval, or deployment operations.

jobs.title: Learning & Development Lead, Operations
jobs.description:
Learning & Development Lead — Operations

Role Overview

The Learning & Development Lead owns training and readiness for Physical Intelligence's robot operator workforce.

This person is responsible for designing and running the systems that take a new operator from candidate work trial through their first 30–60 days, with the goal of getting people productive quickly while maintaining a high quality bar.

They also own ongoing training as the work changes. When researchers introduce new robot workflows, tasks, tools, or operating procedures, the Learning & Development Lead translates those changes into training that can be rolled out quickly and consistently across the operation.

This is a highly operational training role. We are looking for someone who has built or owned training programs for hourly or frontline employees and knows how to turn complex work into a simple, repeatable learning process.



Responsibilities

Operator Trials & Readiness

 - Own the operator work-trial program and ensure candidates are evaluated consistently.

 - Maintain clear trial standards, evaluator guidance, and scoring criteria.

 - Partner with recruiting and operations to continuously improve what the trial predicts about future operator success.

New-Hire Onboarding

 - Build and run onboarding from day one through the first 30–60 days.

 - Define what an operator should know and be able to do at each stage of ramp.

 - Create training plans, checklists, certification steps, and readiness milestones.

 - Identify struggling operators early and create clear paths for remediation.

 - Continuously improve time-to-productivity for new hires.

New Workflow Training

 - Partner with researchers and operations teams when new robot tasks, systems, or processes are introduced.

 - Learn new workflows quickly and translate them into clear training materials and operating instructions.

 - Design the rollout plan needed to train a large operator population quickly.

 - Track who has been trained and verify that the training actually resulted in correct execution.

 - Maintain consistency as training expands across shifts, teams, and locations.

Training Operations

 - Maintain a clear training calendar and ensure training happens when required.

 - Coordinate trainers, operators, shift leads, and researchers.

 - Keep training materials current as workflows change.

 - Build repeatable processes so training does not depend on tribal knowledge.

 - Track training completion, readiness, and performance metrics.

Continuous Improvement

 - Use operator performance data and feedback to identify gaps in training.

 - Work with operations leaders to understand recurring quality or productivity issues.

 - Determine whether problems are caused by training, instructions, process, tooling, or something else.

 - Continuously simplify and improve how operators learn.

What We're Looking For

 - Experience owning training, onboarding, or workforce development programs for hourly or frontline employees.

 - Demonstrated ability to get new employees productive quickly.

 - Experience building structured ramp programs with clear milestones and standards.

 - Strong operational organization and follow-through.

 - Able to turn ambiguous or technical workflows into simple, teachable processes.

 - Comfortable managing trainers, who are responsible for training large groups of people on new procedures under tight timelines.

 - Strong written and verbal communication.

 - Able to work effectively with both highly technical stakeholders, trainers, and frontline operators.

 - Comfortable in an environment where processes and requirements change frequently.

 - Uses data and observation to improve training rather than relying only on subjective feedback.

Experience in robotics is not required.
